Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. JUN 2 2 2010 ATTY. OCTAVIUS L. LABTIC President Vice-Mayor's League of the Philippines (VMLP) Leyte Chapter Dear Atty. Labtic: 92 s. 2010 This has reference to your earlier letter asking our legal opinion on the following queries, to wit: "1. Whether or not a Municipal Vice-Mayor in traveling outside the municipality, such as, attending meetings, congresses, and Conventions of the Vice-Mayor;s League of the Philippines (VMLP), requires the issuance of a travel order from his chief executive even if the funds in defraying his traveling expenses is chargeable against the funds of the sangguniang bayan wherein the latter maintains a separate account. 2. Whether or not a Municipal Accountant is justified in refusing to process pre-payment of official travel of a municipal vice-mayor on the ground that the Municipal Mayor concerned did not issue a travel order." In reply thereto, please be informed that this Department had already answered similar queries in DILG Opinion No. 05, series of 2004. Anent your first query, we opined in the aforesaid legal opinion that the Municipal Mayor, being the chief executive who exercise general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services and activities of the municipal government, is given the sole prerogative to authorize official trips outside of the municipality of municipal officials and employees. This is part and parcel of the executive function of the municipal mayor. It becomes a duty on the part of the municipal mayor to authorize trips, including the issuance of corresponding travel orders therefore to members of the sangguniang bayan and its employees whenever the municipal vice-mayor had already issued his prior recommendation thereto and had already signed the warrant drawn on the municipal treasury for all expenditures necessary for such official travel chargeable to the sanggunian fund. With regard to your second query, we also opined in the aforesaid legal opinion that after the lapse of 15 days from the time the Municipal Mayor received the request for issuance of travel order under his ministerial duty, the

-2- Municipal Budget Office and the Municipal Accounting Office could lawfully and validly facilitate the cash advance of the sanggunian officials and its emplyees. Hereto attached is a photocopy of the aforesaid DILG Opinion for your ready perusal. Thank you and warm regards. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MFD ESUS B.
